title: PLAS: Latent Action Space for Offline Reinforcement Learning

methods.one_paragraph_description: Train a CVAE on the dataset to model the behavior policy p(a|s); then train a deterministic latent policy z = pi(s) (tanh output scaled by 'max latent action') with DDPG/TD3-style deterministic policy gradient and clipped double Q-learning, and decode actions with the fixed pretrained CVAE decoder p_beta(a|s,z). The latent policy's bounded output keeps the decoded actions within the support of the behavior policy. No perturbation layer.
methods.conventional_lineage_hint: offline RL / batch RL with implicit policy constraint ('We propose a straightforward approach to offline RL that implicitly constrains the policy to be within the support of the dataset without being restricted by the density of the dataset distribution.')

methods.one_paragraph_description: PLAS plus an optional perturbation layer on top of the decoder output that outputs a residual over the action limited to [-epsilon, epsilon] (L-infinity), allowing controlled out-of-distribution actions when the Q-function generalizes well. Inspired by BCQ's perturbation model but applied to a deterministic latent policy.

D4RL dataset version (v0/v2) never stated; env names '-v2' refer to Gym environments. The remark that hopper-medium-expert was medium-replay+expert in 'the current version of the d4rl dataset' and the two variants (a)/(b) are recorded as separate dataset rows.
No standard deviations reported in Tables 1-3; only training curves (Figure 4) show shaded std.

PLAS+P 'main' column in Table 3 is the best over the max-perturbation sweep ('we report the best result from Appendix D'); the winning epsilon per dataset is not tabulated (Figure 7 only). E.g. hopper-medium PLAS+P = 36.9 does not match any Table 1 column, presumably epsilon=0.01 from Figure 7.
Table 1 epsilon=0 column duplicates the PLAS main rows of Table 3 (identical values); not emitted twice.

Table 2 (raw average reward) duplicates Table 3 datasets in raw returns; not extracted as rows since normalized scores exist in Table 3.
